text:
If eyes could attain

to discover the immense sorrow

of the red stars,

on heaven’s summit

they would find you among the holy multitude.


You, alone, lend to the heavens, brighter than the sun, your halo:

gold transformed into the splendid corolla

which struck terror in the Moor.


O land governed

by your sacred and victorious scepter,

as it saw itself raised high!

O fortunate people,

O glorious throne of Iberia!


For you that noble endeavor

crowned the Christian people with fame;

for you, master of the sea,

the sovereign genius

found a new world in the Ocean.


But to your soul

two worlds on earth were narrow space,

and toward a third palm

to conquer by right

your spirit rose still farther.


Queen and saint alike,

from majesty to majesty you rose,

and reached where

the sun itself rises,

and seated yourself above the stars.


O sacred one! O great matron

of the Christian flock! O my queen!

Be for the crown

you once sustained

an invincible shelter and pious guardian.


Bless and encourage

the adored, childlike, pure head

that wears your diadem today,

and beneath the tenderness

of your divine love may it grow secure.

translation.title: To Isabella the Catholic
translation.editorial_note: Translated from the stored Spanish original. The royal-Catholic rhetoric and historical claims are retained as the speaker’s address.
